subject: chemistry
title: Model Question Paper 3
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 80 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.

MCQs carry 1 mark; objective questions carry 2 marks (two parts of 1 mark each); very short answers carry 2 marks (30–50 words); short answers 3 marks (50–80 words); long answers 5 marks (80–120 words).
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Write (a) the relationship between K_a and K_b of a conjugate pair and (b) the Henderson equation for an acidic buffer.
questions.answer: (a) K_a × K_b = K_w. (b) pH = pK_a + log([salt]/[acid]).

questions.q: Name (a) the anode and (b) the cathode in the Daniell cell.
questions.answer: (a) Zinc electrode (oxidation, negative). (b) Copper electrode (reduction, positive).

questions.q: Complete the reactions: (a) 2Na + 2H2O → ______ (b) CaCO3 → (heat) ______.
(a) Which is the most electronegative element? (b) Write its electronic configuration.
Complete and balance: (a) XeF6 + 2H2O → ______ (b) NaCl + conc. H2SO4 (423 K) → ______.

questions.answer: (a) Anhydrous ZnCl2 and conc. HCl. (b) Tertiary alcohol (turbidity appears at once).

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Why are BaSO4 and SrSO4 insoluble while BeSO4 and MgSO4 are soluble?
questions.answer: Down the group, the hydration enthalpy decreases faster than the lattice enthalpy; for the large cations Ba^2+ and Sr^2+ the lattice enthalpy dominates, so sulphates are insoluble.

questions.q: What is meant by catenation? Name the p-block element showing it most.
questions.answer: The ability of an element to form bonds with atoms of the same element, producing chains and rings; carbon shows it most because of the strong C–C bond.

questions.q: What are interhalogen compounds? Give two examples.
questions.answer: Compounds formed between two different halogens, e.g. ClF3 and IF7.

questions.q: Why are transition metals and their compounds often coloured?
questions.answer: The partially filled d orbitals split in energy in the presence of ligands, and electrons absorb visible light for d–d transitions; the transmitted complementary colour is observed.

questions.q: What is meant by linkage isomerism? Give an example.
questions.answer: Isomerism due to ambidentate ligands that can attach through different donor atoms. [Co(NH3)5NO2]^2+ (N-bonded nitro) and [Co(NH3)5ONO]^2+ (O-bonded nitrito).

questions.q: Write the IUPAC names of CH3CH2SH and CH3CH2CHO.
Why is benzene less reactive in addition but gives substitution reactions?
questions.answer: The delocalised π electron cloud gives great resonance stability (about 150 kJ mol^-1); addition would destroy aromaticity, whereas substitution retains it.

questions.q: Distinguish between SN1 and SN2 reactions (two points).
questions.answer: SN1: two steps through a carbocation, rate depends on [RX] only, racemisation, tertiary halides favoured. SN2: single step, rate depends on [RX][Nu], inversion of configuration, primary halides favoured.

questions.q: Why do alcohols have higher boiling points than ethers of comparable molecular mass?
questions.answer: Alcohols form intermolecular hydrogen bonds; ethers cannot form hydrogen bonds among themselves.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Differentiate between molarity, molality and mole fraction.
questions.answer: Molarity = moles of solute per litre of solution (changes with temperature). Molality = moles of solute per kg of solvent (independent of temperature). Mole fraction = moles of a component divided by total moles (no unit, independent of temperature).

questions.q: State three applications of coordination compounds.
questions.answer: EDTA is used to estimate Ca^2+ and Mg^2+ (hardness) and in lead poisoning; cis-platin is an anticancer drug; extraction of silver and gold by cyanide complexes; haemoglobin, chlorophyll and vitamin B12 are coordination compounds.

questions.q: Explain the mechanism of the SN2 reaction of CH3Br with OH−.
questions.answer: The nucleophile OH− attacks the carbon from the side opposite to Br (backside) in a single step through a transition state in which C is partly bonded to both OH and Br; Br− leaves and the configuration is inverted; rate = k[CH3Br][OH−].

questions.q: Compare the basic strength of ammonia, methylamine, dimethylamine and aniline and give reasons.
questions.answer: Dimethylamine > methylamine > ammonia > aniline in basicity: alkyl groups donate electrons (+I) and increase the availability of the lone pair; aniline's lone pair is delocalised into the ring.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: (a) Describe the preparation and chemical reactions of ethers. (b) Why are ethers soluble in water but have low boiling points? (c) Write the IUPAC names of CH3OCH2CH3 and C6H5OCH3.
questions.answer:
(a) Prepared by dehydration of alcohol (413 K, excess alcohol) and Williamson synthesis. Reactions: cleavage with HI (R–O–R' + HI → RI + R'OH), electrophilic substitution of aromatic ethers (anisole gives o/p products) and peroxide formation in air.
(b) The oxygen forms hydrogen bonds with water, but there is no hydrogen bonding among ether molecules, giving low boiling points.
(c) Methoxyethane and methoxybenzene (anisole).

questions.q: (a) Classify carbohydrates with examples. (b) Explain the structure of glucose (open chain and cyclic). (c) Why is glucose called a reducing sugar?
questions.answer:
(a) Monosaccharides (glucose, fructose), disaccharides (sucrose, maltose, lactose) and polysaccharides (starch, cellulose, glycogen).
(b) Open chain: HOCH2–(CHOH)4–CHO, an aldohexose; in the cyclic form the –CHO at C-1 reacts with the –OH at C-5 to give a six-membered pyranose ring (α- and β-anomers).
(c) It has a free aldehyde (hemiacetal) group which reduces Tollens' and Fehling's reagents.
